29326:
Kinetic energy is K = \frac{1}{2} m v^2, so mass contributes once and speed twice to the fractional error
\frac{\Delta K}{K} = \frac{\Delta m}{m} + 2 \frac{\Delta v}{v} = 2 \% + 2 \times 3 \% = 8 \%
A maximum error of 8 \% matches option A → (A)
29327:
Velocity is v = \frac{dx}{dt} = 6 t^2 - 18 t + 12, and rest means v = 0
Dividing by 6 gives t^2 - 3 t + 2 = 0, with roots t_1 = 1 s and t_2 = 2 s
Their sum is t_1 + t_2 = 3 s, matching option A → (A)
29328:
Start from the full disc, whose moment of inertia about the central perpendicular axis is \frac{1}{2} M R^2
Each cut-out circle of mass m at centre distance d contributes \frac{1}{2} m r^2 + m d^2 by the parallel axis theorem
Removing four such circles leaves \frac{1}{2} M R^2 - 4 (\frac{1}{2} m r^2 + m d^2), which is option A → (A)
29331:
With the Zener removed, the divider gives V_0 = V_{in} \frac{R_L}{R_s + R_L} = 10 \times \frac{2}{3} V, about 6.67 V
This exceeds the breakdown voltage V_Z = 6 V, so the Zener conducts and clamps the output
The regulated output is therefore V_0 = 6 V, option A → (A)
29332:
Microwaves suit radar and ovens, infrared suits remote controls, ultraviolet suits water purifiers and X-rays suit medical imaging
So (A) - (I), (B) - (II), (C) - (III), (D) - (IV) holds, which is option A → (A)
29333:
Acceleration is a = \frac{F}{m} = \frac{20}{5} = 4 \text{ m / s}^2 from rest
Distance covered in 3 s is s = \frac{1}{2} a t^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 9 = 18 m
Work is W = F s = 20 \times 18 = 360 \text{ J}, option A → (A)
29337:
Photoelectric equation gives e V_0 = h 
u - \phi for frequency 
u
At doubled frequency e V_0' = 2 h 
u - \phi = 2 (e V_0 + \phi) - \phi = 2 e V_0 + \phi
Since \phi is positive, V_0' is greater than 2 V_0, option A → (A)
29338:
Bending splits the wire into two semicircular branches, each of resistance R / 2
Diametrically opposite points put these branches in parallel
Equivalent resistance is \frac{(R / 2) \times (R / 2)}{R / 2 + R / 2} = \frac{R}{4}, option A → (A)
29340:
Current I in inductance L stores magnetic energy U = \frac{1}{2} L I^2
This matches option A → (A)
29341:
In a step-up transformer the secondary has more turns, so secondary voltage rises while secondary current falls
Power and frequency stay unchanged, so the quantity that increases is voltage, option A → (A)
29345:
Gauss law gives flux \Phi_E = \frac{q_{enc}}{\varepsilon_0} through any closed surface
The dipole encloses +q and -q together, so q_{enc} = +q - q = 0
Hence the total flux is zero, option A → (A)
29347:
Fall time is t_1 = \sqrt{\frac{2 h}{g}} = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 20}{10}} = 2 s
Sound return takes t_2 = \frac{h}{v_s} = \frac{20}{340} s, about 0.0588 s
Total t = 2.0588 s = 205.88 \times 10^{-2} s, rounding to x = 206 → (206)
29348:
After 87.5 \% decays, 12.5 \% remains, and 12.5 \% = \frac{1}{8} = (\frac{1}{2})^3
Three half-lives have passed, so t = 3 \times 10 = 30 days
Hence the required time is 30 days → (30)
29351:
Dacron is a polyester assembled from ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid with a water molecule lost at each new linkage
Such growth with elimination of a small molecule defines condensation polymerisation
Polythene, polystyrene and Teflon all grow by addition across a carbon double bond with nothing eliminated
Only Dacron belongs to the condensation class → (A)
29352:
Let the oxidation state of nickel in the complex be x
Each carbonyl CO ligand is neutral and contributes 0 to the charge sum
The complex is neutral overall, so x + 4 \times 0 = 0, giving x = 0 → (A)
29353:
VSEPR electron counting gives \text{BF}_{3} three bond pairs with trigonal planar shape
\text{CH}_{4} has four bond pairs with tetrahedral shape
\text{PCl}_{5} has five bond pairs with trigonal bipyramidal shape, while \text{SF}_{6} has six bond pairs with octahedral shape
Matching gives (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III) and (D)-(IV) → (A)
29354:
Fehling's test is answered only by reducing sugars carrying a free aldehyde or hemiacetal group
Maltose is a reducing disaccharide with one free hemiacetal end
Sucrose locks both anomeric carbons in its glycosidic bond so it is non-reducing, and starch and cellulose are non-reducing polysaccharides
Only maltose gives a positive test → (A)
29356:
Alcoholic KOH abstracts a beta hydrogen while bromide leaves in a single E2 elimination step
2-bromopropane can only expel HBr to build the C = C bond of propene
Aqueous KOH would instead substitute the bromide to give propan-2-ol, but alcoholic medium favours elimination
The major product is therefore propene → (A)
29357:
Visible colour in transition metal ions needs a d-d electron transition, hence a partly filled d subshell
\text{Sc}^{3+} has the configuration 3d^{0} with no d electron available to excite
\text{Ti}^{3+} is 3d^{1}, \text{Cu}^{2+} is 3d^{9} and \text{Fe}^{3+} is 3d^{5}, so all three are coloured
Only \text{Sc}^{3+} is colourless → (A)
29358:
Write the rate law as rate = k[A]^{n} with order n
Raising the concentration fourfold multiplies the rate by 4^{n}
The observed doubling gives 4^{n} = 2, hence 2^{2n} = 2^{1} and 2n = 1
Order is therefore n = 1 / 2 → (A)
29359:
All standard electrode potentials are measured against the standard hydrogen electrode as reference
By international convention this reference half cell is assigned zero potential at every temperature
Hence E^{\circ} = 0.00 V → (A)
29360:
The carbylamine test needs a primary amine reacting with \text{CHCl}_{3} + KOH to form the foul smelling isocyanide
Aniline \text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{5}\text{NH}_{2} is a primary aromatic amine
N-methylaniline is secondary, N,N-dimethylaniline is tertiary, and nitrobenzene carries no amino group at all
Only aniline answers the test → (A)
29361:
Xenon brings 8 valence electrons and bonds to 4 fluorines, leaving 2 lone pairs on xenon
Steric number is 4 + 2 = 6, so electron geometry is octahedral
The two lone pairs occupy trans axial positions to minimise mutual repulsion
The four fluorines then mark out a square plane → (A)
29362:
Carius estimation precipitates bromine as AgBr of molar mass 188 g mol^{-1}
Moles of AgBr are 0.188 / 188 = 0.001, so bromine mass is 0.001 \times 80 = 0.08 g
Percentage of bromine is 0.08 / 0.2 \times 100 = 40\%
This value is the first listed option → (A)
29363:
Greenhouse gases warm the atmosphere by absorbing outgoing infrared radiation through IR-active vibrations
\text{CO}_{2}, \text{CH}_{4} and \text{O}_{3} all possess such modes
\text{N}_{2} is a homonuclear diatomic with no IR-active vibration and traps no heat
Hence \text{N}_{2} is not a greenhouse gas → (A)
29364:
The -COOCH_{3} end is a methyl ester, fixing methyl as the alkyl prefix
Counting the carbonyl carbon, the longest acid chain has 4 carbons, giving a butanoate parent
A methyl branch sits on carbon 3 numbered from the carbonyl carbon
The systematic name is methyl 3-methylbutanoate → (A)
29365:
Square planar [\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_{3})_{2}\text{Cl}_{2}] can place its two ammonia ligands adjacent or opposite
Adjacent placement is the cis isomer and opposite placement is the trans isomer
No third distinct arrangement exists for two pairs of identical ligands
Geometric isomers total 2 → (A)
29366:
Intensive properties do not depend on the amount of matter present
Density is the ratio of mass to volume and stays unchanged when the system is subdivided
Volume, mass and enthalpy each scale with system size and are extensive
Density alone is intensive → (A)
29367:
Benzaldehyde has no alpha hydrogen, so concentrated NaOH triggers Cannizzaro disproportionation
One aldehyde molecule is oxidised to sodium benzoate while a second is reduced to benzyl alcohol
The two products arise in equal amounts from two molecules of aldehyde
The product pair is benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate → (A)
29369:
Neutral \text{FeCl}_{3} develops the blood red colour only with the acetate ion
Acetate builds the basic ferric acetate cation [\text{Fe}_{3}(\text{OH})_{2}(\text{CH}_{3}\text{COO})_{6}]^{+}
Phenol instead gives a violet colouration, while formic and benzoic acids give no blood red colour
Acetate alone fits the observation → (A)
29370:
Frenkel defect shifts a small cation into an interstitial site and leaves its lattice site vacant
\text{Ag}^{+} is much smaller than \text{Cl}^{-}, so it slips into interstitial voids easily
Schottky disorder needs similarly sized ions with paired vacancies, while metal excess and impurity defects are non-stoichiometric
AgCl therefore exhibits Frenkel defect → (A)
29371:
\text{XeF}_{2} bonds xenon to 2 fluorines and leaves 3 lone pairs on xenon
Each fluorine atom carries 3 lone pairs of its own
Total lone pairs are 3 + 2 \times 3 = 9
Hence the count is 9 → (9)
29372:
Freezing depression obeys \Delta T_{f} = i K_{f} m with \Delta T_{f} = 0.2046, K_{f} = 1.86 and m = 0.1
Van't Hoff factor is i = 0.2046 / (1.86 \times 0.1) = 1.1
For HA dissociating as HA \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^{+} + \text{A}^{-} the factor reads i = 1 + \alpha
Degree of dissociation is \alpha = 0.1 = 1 \times 10^{-1}, so x = 1 → (1)
29373:
The benzene ring contains 6 carbon-carbon links, each contributing one \sigma bond
Each of the 6 ring carbons also carries one C-H \sigma bond
Total is 6 + 6 = 12, with the delocalised \pi system adding no further \sigma bond
Hence the \sigma bond count is 12 → (12)
29374:
First order decay leaves fraction 1 / 10 behind after 90\% decomposition in 60 min
99\% decomposition leaves fraction 1 / 100 = (1 / 10)^{2} behind
Reaching the squared fraction needs two such stages, hence twice the time
Required time is t = 2 \times 60 = 120 min → (120)
29375:
Assign Na as +1 and O as -2 in \text{Na}_{2}\text{S}_{2}\text{O}_{3}
Charge neutrality gives 2 \times (+1) + 2S + 3 \times (-2) = 0
Simplifying yields 2 + 2S - 6 = 0, so 2S = 4
Average oxidation number of sulphur is +2 → (2)
29378:
Apply the Cayley-Hamilton theorem, which says every square matrix satisfies its own characteristic equation
Compute the trace 3 + 2 = 5 and the determinant \det(A) = 3 \times 2 - 1 \times (-1) = 7
Form the characteristic polynomial \lambda^2 - 5 \lambda + 7 = 0
Substitute the matrix for \lambda to obtain A^2 - 5A + 7I = O
Hence the expression is the zero matrix, which is option A → (A)
29379:
For a parametric curve use \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/d\theta}{dx/d\theta}
Differentiate to get \frac{dx}{d\theta} = -3a \cos^2 \theta \sin \theta and \frac{dy}{d\theta} = 3a \sin^2 \theta \cos \theta
Divide the derivatives to obtain \frac{dy}{dx} = -\tan \theta
Evaluate at \theta = \frac{\pi}{4}, where \tan \theta = 1, so the tangent slope is -1
A normal is perpendicular, so its slope m satisfies m \times (-1) = -1, giving m = 1
This matches option A → (A)
29381:
Denote the integral by I = \int_0^{\pi/2} \ln(\tan x) dx
Apply the reflection property \int_0^a f(x) dx = \int_0^a f(a - x) dx with a = \frac{\pi}{2}
This gives I = \int_0^{\pi/2} \ln(\tan(\frac{\pi}{2} - x)) dx = \int_0^{\pi/2} \ln(\cot x) dx
Since \cot x = \frac{1}{\tan x}, the logarithm changes sign and I = -I
Hence 2I = 0, so I = 0
This value matches option A → (A)
29382:
Read the coefficients with Vieta: \alpha + \beta = 5 and \alpha \beta = 6
Use the identity \alpha^2 + \beta^2 = (\alpha + \beta)^2 - 2\alpha\beta
Substitute the known sums to get 5^2 - 2 \times 6
Simplify 25 - 12 = 13
This value matches option A → (A)
29383:
Fill the five places one by one with five distinct digits
Count choices as 5 for the first place, then 4, 3, 2 and 1
Multiply by the counting principle: 5 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1
Evaluate the product to get 120, which is 5!
This count matches option A → (A)
29384:
Use the component formula \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = a_1 b_1 + a_2 b_2 + a_3 b_3
Substitute the components to get 3 \times 1 + 2 \times 2 + 2 \times (-2)
Multiply term by term to obtain 3 + 4 - 4
Add the terms to get 3
This value matches option A → (A)
29385:
Use the parallel-plane distance formula \frac{|d_1 - d_2|}{\sqrt{a^2 + b^2 + c^2}}
Read off d_1 = 3 and d_2 = -6 with normal direction (1, 2, 2)
Compute the numerator |3 - (-6)| = 9
Compute the denominator \sqrt{1 + 4 + 4} = \sqrt{9} = 3
Divide \frac{9}{3} = 3, which matches option A → (A)
29387:
Recall the principal range of \cos^{-1} is [0, \pi]
Since -\frac{1}{2} < 0, the value lies in the second quadrant
Split the negative argument as \cos^{-1}\left( -\frac{1}{2} \right) = \pi - \cos^{-1}\left( \frac{1}{2} \right)
Use \cos^{-1}\left( \frac{1}{2} \right) = \frac{\pi}{3} to get \pi - \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{2\pi}{3}
This value matches option A → (A)
29388:
Apply the addition theorem P(\text{spade or ace}) = P(\text{spade}) + P(\text{ace}) - P(\text{both})
Count 13 spades and 4 aces, with 1 card common to both groups
Favourable cards number 13 + 4 - 1 = 16 out of 52
Simplify \frac{16}{52} = \frac{4}{13}
This probability matches option A → (A)
29389:
Compare with the standard ellipse \frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1, whose major axis is 2a when a > b
Read a^2 = 36 and b^2 = 25, so a = 6 and b = 5
Since 6 > 5, the major axis runs in the x direction
Compute its length 2 \times 6 = 12
This value matches option A → (A)
29390:
Square the base first: (1 + i)^2 = 1 + 2i + i^2 = 2i
Raise both sides to the fourth power: (1 + i)^8 = ((1 + i)^2)^4 = (2i)^4
Separate the factors as 2^4 \times i^4
Use i^4 = 1 to get 16 \times 1 = 16
Hence k = 16, which matches option A → (A)
29391:
Recall the symmetric form \frac{x - x_1}{a} = \frac{y - y_1}{b} = \frac{z - z_1}{c} for a line through (x_1, y_1, z_1)
Insert the point (1, 2, 3) so the numerators read x - 1, y - 2 and z - 3
Insert the direction ratios (2, 3, 6) as the denominators
Assemble \frac{x - 1}{2} = \frac{y - 2}{3} = \frac{z - 3}{6}
This equation matches option A → (A)
29394:
Multiply each of \frac{1}{bc}, \frac{1}{ca} and \frac{1}{ab} by the nonzero constant abc
The products are a, b and c, which form an AP by hypothesis
Scaling every term of an AP by one nonzero constant always yields another AP
Hence the three reciprocal expressions are in AP
This conclusion matches option A → (A)
29395:
Compare with the standard hyperbola \frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1, whose transverse axis is 2a
Read a^2 = 25 and b^2 = 16, so a = 5
Locate the vertices at (-5, 0) and (5, 0)
Measure the distance between them as 2 \times 5 = 10
This length matches option A → (A)
29396:
Recall the cube-sum identity \sum_{r=1}^n r^3 = \left( \sum_{r=1}^n r \right)^2
Denote the unknown sum by S = \sum_{r=1}^n r, so S^2 = 441
Take square roots to get S = 21 or S = -21
Reject the negative root since a sum of positive integers is positive
Keep S = 21 as the required sum → (21)
29397:
Recall that \sin \theta = 1 exactly when \theta = \frac{\pi}{2} + 2k\pi for integer k
Put \theta = 2x to get 2x = \frac{\pi}{2} + 2k\pi, hence x = \frac{\pi}{4} + k\pi
With k = 0 obtain x = \frac{\pi}{4}, which lies in [0, 2\pi]
With k = 1 obtain x = \frac{5\pi}{4}, also inside, while k = 2 already exceeds 2\pi
Exactly two values qualify, so the number of solutions is → (2)
29398:
Recall the tangent slope is the derivative at the point: m = \left. \frac{dy}{dx} \right|_{x = 2}
Differentiate term by term to get \frac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2 - 6x
Substitute x = 2 to obtain m = 3 \times 4 - 6 \times 2
Simplify 12 - 12 = 0
Hence the required slope is → (0)
29399:
Find the antiderivative by the power rule: \int x^2 dx = \frac{x^3}{3} + C
Insert the limits 0 and 3 to write \left[ \frac{x^3}{3} \right]_0^3
Evaluate at the upper limit: \frac{27}{3} = 9, and at zero the term is 0
Subtract 9 - 0 = 9
Hence the value of the integral is → (9)
29400:
Recall that the mean equals the sum of the observations divided by their count
Add the data: 2 + 4 + 6 + 8 + x = 20 + x across 5 observations
Set the mean expression equal to 5: \frac{20 + x}{5} = 5
Multiply out to get 20 + x = 25, so x = 25 - 20 = 5
Hence the missing observation is → (5)
